## October Caucasus traffic — Kress, Westernhagen and a shipment for Poti

**Sources on this page:** p68 A1, p68 A2.

**Related source pages:** [p69 A](069.md#source-p69-a), [p69 B1](069.md#source-p69-b1), [p69 B2](069.md#source-p69-b2), [p70 A1](070.md#source-p70-a1), [p70 A2](070.md#source-p70-a2), [p71 A1](071.md#source-p71-a1), [p72 A1](072.md#source-p72-a1), [p72 A2](072.md#source-p72-a2), [p72 A3](072.md#source-p72-a3), [p72 B](072.md#source-p72-b).

<a id="edition-cases-caucasus-october-caucasus-october-caucasus-traffic--kress-westernhagen-and-a-shipment-for-poti"></a>


[Source and verification](../experiments/october_caucasus/README.md)

**Source edition and repair analysis:** icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro. **Earlier key:** the published 4–6 October square and 22-column transposition, credited to Childs and George Lasry / Lasry, Niebel, Kopal and Wacker in the [key catalogue](../data/keys.json).

Twelve source records cover seven exchanges about the Caucasus: personnel and money for Kress's delegation, price instructions to Westernhagen, electrical equipment sent to Tiflis, a cargo leaving Braila for Poti, radio timings, a liaison officer and equipment procurement. The p68 procurement pair has a **provisional, heavily repaired first part and a partially extended second part**; it is not a direct recovery of the complete exchange. Another interrupted continuation is retained separately without an accepted reading. The German readings below use explicit editorial repairs. Every received coordinate, surviving garble, ambiguous layout and repair cost is retained in the [certificate](../experiments/october_caucasus/certificates.json). This is a new reproducible edition in this repository, without a first-historical-decipherment claim.

**Display notes:** The German readings use the stated edited witnesses. Square brackets identify a supplied spelling, a proposed value or an explicitly described unresolved passage; the nearby record notes give the category. Uninterpreted literal fields are shown in code, not promoted to names or quantities. A bracketed whole value does not mean that all its characters are unknown.

### p68 A — Provisional procurement text carrying CHI labels

**Source:** printed p68 / PDF page 71, section A, two parts. `COS, POT v NKJ (9.19 p.m., October 5th); VON THO 1640 (5) 2 TEILE`. The first part visibly says **CHI-220**. The second says **CHI-186** and then **RICHI-186** on the next line. Those labels are preserved exactly.

The published 4–6 October key gives a recognizable Kress/Tiflis address and equipment vocabulary. This is another warning that the printed `CHI` label alone does not identify the separate key family used by the open/previously open CHI challenges. These parts are not companions under the recovered p153 key.

<a id="edition-cases-caucasus-october-caucasus-provisional-first-part-reading"></a>

#### Provisional first-part reading

**Readable German:**

> General v. Kress, Tiflis. Zu T-Spruch Nr. [?159; damaged reference]. Betr. Entsendung 2 Offz. nach Tiflis zum Ankauf von Ausrüstungsstücken [continued in part 2]

**Meaning under the proposed repairs:** The message concerns sending two officers to Tiflis to purchase equipment. Its reference number and date cannot be completed responsibly from this edition.

The literal **220-slot** body has **22 coordinate erasures**, including the non-coordinate letters `W` and `K`, and fixes **89/110 raw positions**. Two erased coordinates fall in the same plaintext pair. Its unchanged inverse is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
G?NE??LOKR?SSXTIFL?LXX?1TSP?UC6NR?159F????9XBZTRW?NT?1?DU?G2OFFX0NAUHDTCFSISXZU??XKAUFVONA5SR5?STUNAS?TS?CKENX
```

</details>

The displayed ordinary wording needs **24 known-coordinate substitutions and 17 erased-coordinate fills**. This substantial editorial cost is why the reading remains **provisional**. The `T` in `TSPRUCH` survives directly and is not expanded to an asserted original abbreviation. Five date/reference positions and the first position after `NR` remain unassigned in the proposed template. No precise reference date is supplied.

<a id="edition-cases-caucasus-october-caucasus-limited-second-part-continuation"></a>

#### Limited second-part continuation

Part 2 has exactly **186 slots**, with **41 coordinate erasures** and **56/93 fixed raw positions**. Its beginning `??DARTILLER??T7QITJO?` supports the provisional continuation:

**Readable German:**

> [continued from part 1] und Artilleriemunition [remaining text unresolved]

The bracketed continuation and unresolved-text notices are display descriptions, not recovered German words or a new gap-length hypothesis. The earlier template asserts only `UNDARTILLERIEMUNITION`, requiring **four known-coordinate substitutions and five erasure fills**. The remaining **72 plaintext positions are unasserted**. The certificate retains their raw domains, and its arbitrary coordinate fillers for a complete arithmetic round-trip are not promoted to a further sentence, quantity, date or signature.

A [separately priced continuation](../experiments/p68_procurement_continuation/README.md)
now proposes `DONREGIERUNG`, `DORTEINGE?ANGEN`, `HGRUKIEW` and `ROSTOW`.
Retaining the other raw letters, the earlier opening fixes **61/93 positions**;
the common extension reaches **76/93**, with **one additional observed
substitution and 15 printed-mask fills**. All fifteen newly assigned positions
retain an observed half-coordinate. The wholly missing internal verb letter
admits both `EINGEGANGEN` and `EINGELANGEN` at the same two-fill price, giving
77/93 only under either optional completion. `F??`, the fields `?0` and `1??8`,
and the intervening damaged text remain literal. Native messages attest three
individual words; no complete independent copy of this clause is claimed.

<a id="edition-cases-caucasus-october-caucasus-relation-to-the-open-p73-challenge"></a>

### Relation to the open p73 challenge

These messages add readable traffic from the Kress/Caucasus route, with explicit October origin and later interception dates. They supply neither p73's key nor a matching plaintext passage. **p73 remains open**; the source-level repairs here do not decide between its conflicting 26 October and 8 November date layers.

### p72 A — Reinforcements, administrative personnel and money for Kress

**Source:** printed p72 / PDF page 75, section A, three parts. `COS v OSM (--------, October 9th); NR 294 KRESS (6) 2040 3 TLE`. The heading is **6 October 1918**. The clear route is OSM to COS, with Kress named in the header; it does not make Kress the sender.

<a id="edition-cases-caucasus-october-caucasus-most-likely-readable-german"></a>

#### Most likely readable German

**Readable German:**

> Zu Tel. 30.9. `NATEKS` Nr. 8557. 1. Verstärkung der Deleg. von O.H.L. ohne Beteiligung [des] K.M. angeordnet. 2. Mit Bericht vom 8.[?], `4A` Nr. 553 angeford. Verw.-Pers. wird mit Ausnahme der Garnison-Verw.-Beamten — vergl. Tel. 26.[?], [unresolved reference] — zur Verfügung gestellt werden. 3. Notwendiges Geld ist sichergestellt.

**Meaning:** Reinforcement of the delegation has been ordered by Supreme Army Command, without the participation of the office denoted literally by `K.M.`, under the separately priced article completion below. Requested administrative personnel will be made available, except for garrison-administration officials. Necessary money has been secured.

`Deleg.`, `O.H.L.`, `Verw.-Pers.` and `Garnison-Verw.-Beamten` are expanded only in the explanation. The reference text `NATEKS` and several dates and numbers remain unresolved. The article completion below reads raw `X?S` as `DES` before literal `K.M.`; it does not identify a particular ministry or assign the damaged reference digits.

<a id="edition-cases-caucasus-october-caucasus-what-the-three-source-parts-preserve"></a>

#### Source evidence in the three parts

| Part | Literal / interpreted coordinates | Fixed raw positions | Source issue | Additional editorial cost |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- | ---: |
| A1 | 203 / 178 | 88/89 | The second copy of an identical 25-coordinate run is visibly struck out. | Earlier: 1 substitution, no fill; with conditional article: 2 substitutions, 1 fill |
| A2 | 251 / 226 | 108/113 common to both models; 109/113 in one model | An unmarked 25-slot near-repeat; two deletion alternatives remain. | 6 substitutions; 1 or 2 asserted fills |
| A3 | 124 / 124 | 60/62 | Two invalid/missing source coordinates; unchanged geometry | 4 substitutions; 2 fills |

The A1 strikeout is a source instruction. The A2 deletion is a reconstruction hypothesis: its adjacent copies differ only by a printed `X` versus a non-coordinate `S`. Removing either copy gives the same raw text except for `GARNISON` versus `G?RNISON`. Both are kept; the latter does not become an independently witnessed `A`.

The raw core is already recognizable as `VERSTAER1UNGDERDELEGXVONOXHXLXOHNEBETEILIGUNG...ANGEORDNET`, and A3 directly contains `ZURVERFUEGUN...GESTELLT...` and most of `NOTWENDIGESGELDISTSICHERGESTELLT`. The stated costs account for making those words readable; the uncorrected strings remain in the certificate.

The unchanged inverse ends `OHNEBETEILIGUNGX?SKXMXANGEORDNET`.
A grammatical proposal reads `X?S` as **DES**: “ohne Beteiligung des K.M.
angeordnet”. It adds no plaintext position and changes no source frame.
The source still has D at coordinate 136 and the invalid printed U at 185;
neither glyph is silently retranscribed.

| Plaintext index | Raw pair / label | Proposed label | Additional source operation |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| 72 | `GD` / X | D (`GG`) | source 136 D → G; one observed substitution |
| 73 | `F?` / domain `1EKLOS` | E (`FA`) | source 185 U → A; one invalid-glyph fill |

The 88/89 raw count is unchanged. Including the existing `VERSTAERKUNG`
repair, the conditional first-part layer has **89/89 positions**, at
**two observed-coordinate substitutions and one mask fill**. The printed
25-coordinate strikeout and published key remain exactly as before.

**Readable German — conditional article bracketed, abbreviations retained:**

> Zu Tel. 30.9. NATEKS Nr. 8557. 1. Verstaerkung der Deleg. von O.H.L. ohne Beteiligung [des] K.M. angeordnet.

<summary>Complete conditional first-part machine string</summary>


no institution or separate received copy is asserted.

<a id="edition-cases-caucasus-october-caucasus-p70-a--westernhagen-price-limits-and-an-urgent-return"></a>

### p70 A — Westernhagen, price limits and an urgent return

**Source:** printed p70 / PDF page 73, section A, two parts. `POT, COS v NKJ (3.10 a.m., October 7th); FUR COS DEUTSCHE DELEGATO WIRTCHI ABTLG 2305 (6) 2 TLE`.

<a id="edition-cases-caucasus-october-caucasus-most-likely-readable-german-1"></a>

#### Most likely readable German

**Readable German:**

> An Westernhagen. Bestätigen Telegr. 28.9. Euer früheres Telegr. nicht erhalten. Da von euch ohne Bericht und Kenntnis dortiger Marktlage gelassen, können Preisgrenzen nicht aufgeben. Mdl. Rücksprache sofort erforderlich. Bitten Rück[k]ehr beschleunigen. Drahten Gleiches über ASTO Constanza. Bestätigt Empfang. Deutkauf.

**Meaning:** A telegram of 28 September is acknowledged, but an earlier one was not received. Without the requested report or knowledge of local market conditions, the sender cannot give price limits. An immediate personal discussion is needed; Westernhagen is asked to hasten his return. The same instruction is being telegraphed via `ASTO Constanza`, and receipt is to be acknowledged.

The source names only **Westernhagen**. `MDL` is interpreted as *mündliche*; `ASTO` and the signature `DEUTKAUF` are retained without an institutional expansion. The encrypted spelling is `RUECKEHR` with one `K`; ordinary German spelling in the displayed reading supplies the second `k` as a prose normalization. The unusual but directly decoded `AUFGEBEN` remains; the edition does not silently substitute a more idiomatic verb.

| Part | Literal / interpreted coordinates | Fixed raw positions | Source issue | Additional editorial cost |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- | ---: |
| A1 | 332 / 322 | 156/161 | Two separate identical five-coordinate pairs: `AAAAA AAAAA` and `DAAGG DAAGG` | 7 substitutions; 5 fills |
| A2 | 246 / 246 | 121/123 | Header says `RICHI-256`; the printed 246-slot body decodes at its actual length | 4 substitutions; 2 fills |

Removing one copy of each repeated A1 group gives four source-index aliases and **one identical 322-coordinate stream**. Those deletions are conditional, despite the visible repetition. A2 is not padded by ten invented coordinates to force its length to match the header: its raw reading already begins `MDLXRUECKSPRACHEDOFORTERFORDERLICH...` and ends `...EMPFANGXDEUTKAUF` at 246 slots.

<a id="edition-cases-caucasus-october-caucasus-p71-a1--electrical-equipment-sent-to-tiflis"></a>

### p71 A1 — Electrical equipment sent to Tiflis

**Source:** printed p71 / PDF page 74, section A, first of two parts. `POT v OSM (01.17 a.m., October 8th); FUR COS (6) 1230 2 TEILE; 1 TL RICHI-170`. The page heading is **6 October 1918**.

<a id="edition-cases-caucasus-october-caucasus-most-likely-readable-german-2"></a>

#### Most likely readable German

**Readable German:**

> Nach Tiflis abgegangen 28.9., mit 2 Begleiter: 2 Stück 16-kW-Maschinensätze und 1 [20]-kW-Umformer.

**Meaning:** Two machine sets rated at 16 kW and one converter, provisionally read as rated at 20 kW, were dispatched to Tiflis on 28 September with two accompanying people. The directly decoded telegraphic form is `BEGLEITER`; no grammatical final `N` is inserted into the cipher edition.

The literal **170 slots** have unchanged geometry and fix **72/85 raw positions**. Twelve printed dashes and one damaged `C`-shaped glyph in row one's last group are treated as erasures. That glyph may be an incomplete `G`, but the raw letter domain remains open. The proposed reading fills all **13 erasures** and changes **one known coordinate**, source slot 40 from `G` to `X`, to repair the raw `GEGA?BEN` fragment to `GEGANGEN`. All slot and plaintext positions in the certificate are zero-based.

The two equipment counts, the **16-kW** rating, and the date digits `28` and `9` survive directly. The **2** in the proposed **20-kW** rating is an erasure fill, so the exact second rating is conditional. The raw ending is `...UND1??0KX?XUMFORMER`, not a fully recovered numerical specification.

Part A2 advertises **192 coordinates** but stops after **85**, followed by the printed note `(interference)`. Under the simple hypothesis that the lost suffix supplies the remaining 107 slots, no complete plaintext letter is fixed: each surviving symbol supplies only one side of a coordinate pair. Its literal fragment and conditional letter domains are preserved separately. A [conditional partial edition](071.md#edition-cases-radio-p71-dc-machines-fragment) now proposes a 47-position technical clause with 51 added-slot fills and no observed-coordinate substitutions. Both SCHALTEN and ERHALTEN alternatives remain compatible; the other 49 positions are unread. This proposal does not change the native 0/96 fixed-position count or infer additional equipment specifications.

### p69 B — Violetta's cargo from Braila to Poti

**Source:** printed p69 / PDF page 72, section B, two parts. `COS v NKJ (---- October 11th); NR 298 FUR COS HPTM GEMOLL (6) 2330 2 TLE`. The page heading says **5 October**, while the individual clear header says `(6)`; both are preserved.

<a id="edition-cases-caucasus-october-caucasus-most-likely-readable-german-3"></a>

#### Most likely readable German

**Conditional interpretation — readable German with the separately bracketed cargo/date hypotheses:**

> Ab Braila [4.10.] mit D. Violetta: [10 000] Eierhandgranaten, 3 Wagen Masch.-Gew., `04WLI` russ. Gew., 9 Wag. Mun., `94TS6` Lebensmittel, 16 Faß Benzin, 2 Kisten Kuriergepäck, 10 Wag. Mun. für Mun.-Dep. Poti und mehrere Wag. für dort. Truppen.

**Meaning:** A cargo sent from Braila aboard the vessel *Violetta* includes hand grenades, machine guns, Russian rifles, ammunition, food, petrol and courier luggage. Poti's ammunition depot and troops there are named as destinations. Two damaged quantity fields are unresolved. The proposed **10 000** hand grenades is also conditional: the common raw reading is `100?0`, and the fourth digit depends on the declared alignment and an erased-coordinate fill. It is not an independently established exact quantity.

The displayed **4.10.** date and several words are editorial repairs. `04WLI` and `94TS6` are raw garbles, not accepted quantities; no numerical expansion is supplied for them. `D.`, `Masch.-Gew.`, `russ. Gew.`, `Wag.` and `Mun.-Dep.` are interpreted in their cargo context. The text does not independently establish the ship's registry or the nature of the wagons carried.

| Part | Literal / interpreted coordinates | Raw positions fixed across every tested placement | Source issue | Minimum additional editorial cost |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- | ---: |
| B1 | 329 / 330 | 159/165 | Four-letter group `VXFX`; insert one erased slot at any of its five boundaries | 9 substitutions; 2 fills |
| B2 | 65 / 66 | 28/33 | Four-letter group `(X)FFF`; insert one erased slot at any of its five boundaries | 1 substitution; 1 fill |

These models supply a slot because a printed group is short and the header is one longer. They do not prove that the historical loss occurred there. In B1 the editorial template has two tied minimum-cost placements. In B2, the proposed complete continuation is

```text
UNDMEHREREWAGXFUERDORTXTRUPPENXXX
```

</details>

It replaces the short printed `XFFF` by `GDFFF`: either insert `G` before the printed `X` and change that `X` to `D`, or change `X` to `G` and insert `D` after it. Both have exactly one known-coordinate substitution and one missing-coordinate fill. All five within-group placements, including the more expensive ones, remain in the certificate.

<a id="edition-cases-caucasus-october-caucasus-p72-b--radio-timings-and-reception"></a>

### p72 B — Radio timings and reception

**Source:** printed p72 / PDF page 75, section B. `POT v OSM (---------, October 9th); FUR POT (6) 0830; RIZI-274`. The source prints `RIZI`; that label is not silently rewritten as `RICHI`.

<a id="edition-cases-caucasus-october-caucasus-most-likely-readable-german-4"></a>

#### Most likely readable German

**Readable German:**

> Zu dort Nr. 479: 20.00, 20.30 für OSM ungeeignet. Sind Sie mit RICHI `M98`, 30.9., mitgeteilten Zeiten einverstanden? Wie ist dort Empfang OSM, Welle 2800 und 3500? Schlee.

**Meaning:** The proposed times are unsuitable for OSM. The recipient is asked whether the previously notified times are acceptable and how OSM is received at two wavelengths.

The unchanged 274-coordinate geometry fixes **136/137 raw positions**. The displayed `NR`, `2000`, `SIE` and `3500` require **four known-coordinate substitutions**, with one additional erased-coordinate fill for `ZU`. The first time and second wavelength are plausible editorial values, not independently recovered numerical facts. `2030`, `2800` and `SCHLEE` are directly decoded; the damaged reference `RICHIM98` is left unresolved.

<a id="edition-cases-caucasus-october-caucasus-p69-a--a-liaison-officer-from-army-group-kiev"></a>

### p69 A — A liaison officer from Army Group Kiev

**Source:** printed p69 / PDF page 72, section A. `NKJ v --- (---- October 11th); NR 44 0628 (5.10); RICHI-220`. The sender is not identified in the clear header.

<a id="edition-cases-caucasus-october-caucasus-most-likely-readable-german-5"></a>

#### Most likely readable German

**Readable German:**

> Mit Einverständnis O.H.L. wird Rittm. [Tellner], [Tellner], als Verbdgs.-Offz. der Heeresgr. nach Tiflis entsandt. Heergr. Kjew.

**Meaning:** With Supreme Army Command's approval, a cavalry captain is being sent to Tiflis as the army group's liaison officer. The signature names Army Group Kiev; the cipher's literal spelling is `KJEW`. The two bracketed names are an editorial name reconstruction, not one-position question marks. The damaged surname is repeated and is provisionally read as **Tellner**, without assigning a forename or identifying a person outside the telegram.

The actual body has **220 coordinates**, matching the header. Three parenthesized `X` values are retained as recorded source coordinates, including the final printed run `FDX(X)-X(X)VGX`. Parentheses remain visible in the literal row edition. Removing those annotated letters or treating the ten-slot run as one five-letter group would change the frame.

The literal inverse fixes **109/110 raw positions**:

<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
MITEINVERSTAEWDNISXOXHXLXWIRDRITTMXTELLNEIXTELLN1RXA?SVERBDGSXXBFZDERHEERELGRXNACHXTIKLCSXEN5SAND6XHEERGRXKJEW
```

</details>

The displayed ordinary words require **10 known-coordinate substitutions and one erased-coordinate fill**. The two raw surname copies, `TELLNEI` and `TELLN1R`, preserve complementary letters: `TELLNER` combines the sixth letter of the first copy with the seventh of the second. That is still an editorial reconstruction, not an independent personnel identification. `RITTM`, `VERBDGS` and `OFFZ` are expanded only in the explanation.
